sections.h2: What does a product designer do?
sections.answer: A product designer turns a business goal into a tested feature: they find the user problem, design the flow and the screens, test them and support the build.
sections.body: A UX designer focuses on flows and research. A UI designer focuses on how screens look. A product designer does both and adds product thinking: which problem is worth solving, what to cut, and how to measure success after release. That makes one product designer the right first hire for a small team. Larger teams that need research, UX and UI as separate roles can hire UI UX designers as a team.

sections.h2: When should you hire a product designer?
sections.answer: You should hire a product designer when features ship without a clear user problem behind them, or when engineers wait on design every sprint. These 5 signs show the moment has come:
items: Your roadmap is driven by feature requests, not by measured user problems.
Engineers design screens themselves because no designer is free.
New features look and behave differently from the rest of the product.
You raised a round and need to show product progress within 2 quarters.
You are adding AI features and nobody owns how users will trust and correct them.

sections.h2: How much does it cost to hire a product designer?
sections.answer: Hiring a product designer from us starts at $15,000 per month as part of a dedicated team plan. Seniority and how many designers you add set the final price.
sections.body: One senior product designer paired with a UI designer is the most common starting point. Teams that grow add a researcher or a design lead. For one-off projects with a fixed scope, such as minimum viable product (MVP) design with our MVP design agency team, we quote a fixed price instead. The UI UX design cost guide compares every option.

sections.answer: Answers to common questions before you hire a product designer.

faqs.q: Can I hire a product designer for an AI product?
faqs.a: Yes. Our AI product designers design prompt inputs, generated answers, source previews and correction flows, and test them with real model output.

faqs.q: Do your product designers do user research?
faqs.a: Yes. Every product designer runs interviews and usability tests as part of the work; larger studies add a dedicated UX researcher.

faqs.q: Can a product designer work with our developers directly?
faqs.a: Yes. The designer joins your sprint planning and reviews and hands over specs in Figma that your engineers build from.

faqs.q: What is the difference between a product designer and a UI UX designer?
faqs.a: A UI UX designer focuses on flows and screens; a product designer also decides which problem to solve and how to measure the result after release.
